The Now, Next, Later grid is the third section of the roadmap. It shows the work ahead in three time horizons, one row per goal, so anyone can see what is shipping this quarter, what is coming over the next two quarters, and which problems we are still exploring.

## When

- **Rebuilt at quarterly planning** (step 3, Plan the quarter). The product manager moves items between columns during the planning sessions, and the grid is final when the team commits.
- **Read all quarter.** The grid does not change between planning sessions. Deliverable status lives in Quarterly commitments and the sprint report.
- **One exception.** If mandated work arrives mid-quarter, the product manager adds it and shows what moved out to make room.

## Who

- **Product manager** owns the grid. They are the only person who moves items between columns, and they make the call at quarterly planning.
- **Product owner** helps slice Solutions into Deliverables and confirms which slices are ready for Now.
- **Development team** and **technical architect** size the Deliverables and confirm the team can finish what goes in Now.
- **UX designer and researcher** brings discovery results, which decide which Solutions move to Next and whether an Initiative continues or closes.
- **Executive steering group** and **advisory group** read the grid at the quarter review. They can question placement but don't move items.

## How it works

### Columns are time horizons, and the items change with distance

**Janna Bastow** (ProdPad) created Now/Next/Later as a roadmap with time horizons instead of dates. That is the first rule: a column says *when*. Now is this quarter, Next is the following two quarters, and Later is anything beyond.

The second rule is Ian Swanson's addition: the items are not like-for-like across columns. The further out something sits, the less concrete it is, and the more it is an opportunity than a plan. This is the difference from a project plan, where the milestone due in two years is the same kind of thing as the one due tomorrow.

| Column | When | What you'd expect to find | Language | Success question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Now** | This quarter | Deliverables, committed | Concrete delivery: what lands in people's hands | Did we deliver it, and does it work? |
| **Next** | The following two quarters | Mostly Solutions, getting concrete | User value: who can now do what | Does it solve the problem we found? |
| **Later** | Beyond two quarters | Initiatives: opportunities, not yet committed | A problem or question, in users' terms | Did we learn enough to decide? |

A large Solution spans horizons. Its slice for this quarter is a Deliverable in Now; the rest of it sits in Next, or in Later if it is more than two quarters away.

### Rows are goals

Each goal gets its own swim lane, so every item shows which goal it advances. Strategic capacity (50% by default) is one share across all goal rows. Don't split it per goal.

Two more rows sit under the goals, each with its capacity share:

- **Technical maintenance** (25% by default): the service levels we keep, such as patch times and uptime, plus any large planned maintenance.
- **Small requests** (25% by default): the response-time commitment. Individual small requests stay on the small request board, owned by the product owner. They never appear as items here.

The split is set each quarter at planning and written on the grid. When it differs from the default, add a line saying why.

### Required work is a tag

Work mandated by law, policy or compliance gets a **Required:** tag. Required is not a column. The item goes in the goal row it touches most and the column for when it is due. A fee set by the Legislature for October is already decided, so it goes in whichever column October falls in. A rule whose effect on users is unclear starts in Later like any other problem.

### How items move

The product manager moves items at quarterly planning, using these rules:

1. **Idea log to Later.** An idea, or a cluster of them, gets framed as an Initiative.
2. **Later to Next.** When an Initiative is expected to be active within the next two quarters. By then it should be getting concrete: Next shows the Solutions it plans to try or build, each naming the Initiative. When an Initiative closes, its cards leave the grid and the lesson goes in its status.
3. **Next to Now.** A slice is sized and committed for this quarter. The Deliverable goes in Now and names its parent Solution. Whatever is left of the Solution stays in Next or Later, by when it is expected.
4. **Out of Now.** Deliverables marked Done in Quarterly commitments come off the grid at the next planning session. Unfinished ones roll forward with a note.
5. **Dropped Solutions come off, and that is said out loud.** When a Solution fails a test or doesn't move the outcome, its card leaves the grid and the Initiative's next Solution takes its place. Nothing moves silently.

Use [Roadmap](/templates/roadmap), section 3, Now, Next, Later grid.

## DMV example
This is the DMV grid at Q1 planning, filled in as section 3 of the DMV example in [Roadmap](/templates/roadmap). It starts from the team's real Q1 grid and fixes six placements that broke the rules above, listed below. The fixes are the lesson.

Q1 runs 60/20/20 instead of the 50/25/25 default. Online renewal has a fixed public launch in Q2, and the team cleared its maintenance backlog in Q4, so Strategic gets the extra share this quarter.

Three Initiatives are active in Q1, one per goal: **Online vehicle renewal**, **Real-time eligibility verification** and **Counter staff on complex cases**. Each card names its Solution and Initiative.

What changed from the original Q1 grid:

1. **Digital Identity Verification moved from Next to Now.** It's committed this quarter, so it is a Deliverable. The original kept it in Next under Goal 1, while Quarterly commitments listed it as Q1 work.
2. **Staff Training Program moved from the Goal 2 row to Goal 3.** It gets staff ready, which is Goal 3's intended progress.
3. **"Improve renewal on mobile devices" and "Streamline title transfer process" left Later.** Both were worded as solutions in the horizon where items should still be questions. Title transfer was folded into the complex-transactions question. Mobile went back to the idea log until someone can say what problem it solves.
4. **"Why do users abandon online applications?" moved from Goal 3 to Goal 1.** Abandonment is about finishing online, not about staff.
5. **"Enable self-service address changes" left Next.** No Initiative had chosen it, so it went back into the complex-transactions question in Later, where moving to Oregon is one of the trips to explore.
6. **The two Required items left their own row.** The donor check law fixes what to build, so it goes straight to Now in the goal row it touches. The accessibility audit keeps the service compliant, so it sits in Technical maintenance.

What the grid tells you:

- **Goal 3's Initiative is trying only one Solution, and nothing is in Later.** Training alone may not change how counter work feels. Expect the staff satisfaction measure to stall after Q1 unless the Initiative tries a second Solution, such as redesigning the counter workflow itself.
- **Goal 2 gets a second Initiative at Q2 planning.** "Single-trip new driver licenses" is framed from a counter clerk's idea in January. Its first Solution, a document checklist, is dropped after testing in Q2. By Q3 planning its second, License Ready Check, is in Next with its first slice in Now (see Initiatives and solutions, and Discovery).

## Rules of thumb

- **If you can't name it specifically, it isn't ready for the grid.** "Improve customer experience" doesn't belong in Later. "Why do 40% of applicants call for help instead of finishing online?" does.
- **One thing, one card.** "Phase 1" in Now, "Phase 2" in Next and "Phase 3" in Later is the same item said three times. A Deliverable in Now and its parent Solution in Next are different artifacts, and that's fine.
- **Don't ask Later for a date.** An Initiative owes you a decision, not a ship date.
- **Check concreteness against the horizon.** Something due within two quarters that is still only a question needs discovery started now. Something detailed and specific sitting in Later is a plan pretending to be an opportunity.
- **Read the empty cells.** A goal with nothing in Now won't move this quarter. That should match the intended progress line in Quarterly commitments.
